title: The Stability of God and the Shaking of Nations
english: The Lord is in the midst of her, in the midst of threats (Ps 45:6). There is another scripture saying, 'God will help her with His face.' For He preserves her beauty, which is both vulnerable and incorruptible, the intelligible [beauty]; clearly, the intellect will receive disturbance from opposing things. For when the soul holds faith within itself as unassailable and assigns to itself the refinements of all virtue, the intellect possesses beauty and Christ Himself is revealed to it. Since the immediate, visible, and unchangeable is set aside, the Church, he says, will not be persuaded by this; for He preserves her beauty.

He calls the nations the hordes of demons warring against her (Ps 45:7). And when these see the incarnate appearance of the Savior, they are troubled against His Church and are filled with dread. Furthermore, the falling of the seven kingdoms over which death and sin reigned will follow. Even if you call those reigning 'kingdoms,' they too have fallen, flowing from error into the knowledge of truth and from wickedness into virtue.

Regarding the silence of God, the earthly and material things seem to have stability and standing, being shaken by God's having given a voice (Ps 45:8). For if God assists the intellect, immediately everything earthly is moved. And upon God having given the voice according to the Gospel, the earth has been shaken, with all customs, local laws, useful things, and even the impious deception being changed; the nations are troubled and the kingdoms are falling. While the earth is shaken, we are courageous, having the Lord of powers with us, the God of Jacob taking hold of us (Ps 45:9). Just as he who does the works of Abraham is His child, so he who imitates the asceticism of Jacob becomes His son, having an understanding from the God of Jacob.
And the Holy Spirit calls upon the acute [minds] for the understanding of these things.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
